summary.what_changed: Splits the previously overloaded `partial` state-tracking flag into two distinct signals: `blind` (a blocking agent was prevented from judging its input at all — e.g. source-collector, pr-summarizer, or notifier dispatch failed to produce usable output) and `degraded` (the pipeline judged its input and deliberately withheld or rejected specific content, e.g. a lint block or time-budget truncation). A run classified as blind now exits with a non-zero status code, cannot advance the watermark cursor, and is excluded from the CCE-101 auto-merge gate. Classification happens by call site rather than by matching on reason strings, and every blocking dispatch reason must now be classified — an unclassified failure defaults to blind so it fails loud instead of silently passing as green.
summary.why: Two consecutive nightly runs (31472240064 on 2026-08-11 and 31579090583 on 2026-08-12) reported `conclusion: success` in GitHub Actions even though every subagent was rate-limited and produced no output. Because the orchestrator returned 0 on every code path, this failure mode was invisible, and a subsequent run's watermark advance (PR #215) walked past three PRs (#211/#212/#213) whose documentation content is now permanently unrecoverable. CCE-144 closes that blind spot by making 'the pipeline could not judge its input' a first-class, loudly-failing state distinct from 'the pipeline judged and rejected input,' which must remain non-fatal to avoid reinstating the earlier CCE-109 doom loop.

summary.what_changed: Fixes the docs-agent's page-authoring loop so a nightly run cuts its work at a PR boundary instead of an arbitrary page-batch index. Previously the CCE-109 time-budget check fired at any batch index, and the at-least-one-progress escape hatch (`i > 0`) operated per page-batch rather than per PR. When the oldest PR in a run's window fanned out to more page batches than the time budget could author, the run split that PR's batch group on every single run and never finished authoring it — so the baseline cursor could never advance past it (observed on the ADIS host as a 20.6-day stall, always reporting `time_budget_no_advance_no_cursor`). The fix reworks the authoring loop's cut logic to operate at PR granularity: a run either fully authors a PR's page batches or defers the whole PR, guaranteeing forward progress every run.
summary.why: Root cause per CCE-152/ADIS-515: batch-level truncation combined with a batch-level (not PR-level) progress escape created a doom loop identical in spirit to CCE-109, but scoped to a single oversized PR rather than an oversized window. CCE-140's cursor-backed advance only helps once a PR is fully authored; a PR stuck mid-authoring forever blocks the cursor. Cutting authoring at PR boundaries closes that gap and lets the run's forward progress guarantees hold even for PRs with unusually large page fan-out.

doc_targets.notes: Document the PR-boundary authoring cut: the CCE-109 time-budget check and progress escape now operate per PR rather than per page-batch, closing the CCE-152 doom-loop variant.

summary.what_changed: Fixes the citation_exists Tier-1 lint check so it resolves Python symbol citations (`path:symbol`) against any definition site — methods, nested functions, class attributes — not just top-level module definitions. Previously the linter only recognized symbols defined at the top level of a Python file, so citations to real, correctly-defined symbols nested inside a class or function were incorrectly reported as nonexistent, causing the authored page to be dropped by content-validator. Because a dropped page is not retried and the collection window still advances, this silently and permanently stranded documentation for legitimately-cited code.
summary.why: Root cause per CCE-145: on three consecutive nightly runs against theoju/claude-code-self-assessment, citation_exists produced false positives for exported symbols and gitignored paths, blocking roughly 11 authored pages per run. Because last_successful_run.head_sha advances even when a page is dropped, those pages fell permanently out of the collection range with no re-attempt path. This PR corrects the symbol-resolution logic to eliminate that class of false positive, closing CCE-145 (and is part of the broader CCE-122 line-free citation design plus the CCE-141/CCE-152 related stranding-prevention work).

summary.what_changed: The nightly orchestrator's watermark-advance logic is now cursor-backed on every code path, not just the time-truncated one. `deferred_pages_by_pr` and the `held_back` set are now computed unconditionally, and the cursor walk that limits the advance to the last fully-documented PR is entered whenever `time_truncated OR held_back` is true (previously it was nested only inside the `if time_truncated:` branch). A clean run's behavior is unchanged (full window-HEAD advance when nothing is held back); a run that is partial for a non-time reason (lint block, `page_author_invalid`, etc.) now advances only as far as the last PR whose pages all landed, instead of jumping to full window HEAD and silently discarding the undocumented window. Reason strings are now cause-dependent (`time_budget_*` vs `held_back_*`) to preserve existing operator-facing grep patterns and test assertions for the time-truncated family.
summary.why: CCE-144 built the cursor-backed advance and the `deferred_pages_by_pr` complement writer, but wired the gating check only inside the `if time_truncated:` branch. Any run that was partial for a non-time reason (a lint block or a `page_author_invalid`) fell into the `else` branch, which set `advance_sha = current_run.head_sha` (full window HEAD) without ever reading `deferred_pages_by_pr`. Because the watermark cursor is consume-once, the skipped window was permanently lost and the run still exited 0, so nothing alarmed. This was identified as a known residual ("C1") in CCE-144's own final review and documented in prose but had no ticket until CCE-151. Two incidents (runs 32460602658 and 32495019606 on 2026-08-21) each blocked a page on lint and then advanced past the very window that held the stranded content, requiring a hand-written baseline rewind to recover.

summary.what_changed: The docs-agent now detects citations that page-author shortened into an unresolvable form (e.g. dropping a directory prefix) and reports them as an info-only digest line, instead of attempting to repair them. Detection now runs via _diagnose_citation_paths in orchestrator_runner.py, after the authoring loop and before the lint-block revert, so it inspects the same finished tree citation_exists checks. Findings are bounded per-page and per-run and classified into four confidence labels (candidate_in_run_inputs, suffix_match_only, ambiguous, no_candidate), with only the first three surfaced in the digest.
summary.why: CCE-141: page-author occasionally shortens an already-resolvable citation, and citation_exists correctly blocks the resulting page every run, so the page is silently never written. Measurement against the full archived PR history showed zero real firings that a unique-suffix repair would have resolved, and disabling the feature entirely left the test suite unchanged, so the team kept detection-only and dropped the repair/rewrite path.

summary.what_changed: Fixes a deadlock in the docs-agent nightly orchestrator where the deferral-skip escape hatch (from CCE-140) could never open. The consecutive-deferral counter lives in state.json, which is only updated on merge to main — but the run stays partial and unmerged precisely while the hatch is needed, so the counter never persists and the escape can never arm. The fix introduces a wall-clock-based stall detector: baseline_stall_days reads last_successful_run.completed_at (a durable, external signal unaffected by merge status), and resolve_deferral_stall_days derives a stall window as the deferral threshold plus one, guaranteeing the clock is strictly slower than the counter. When the baseline is older than the stall window, the run forgives the single oldest deferred PR (the cursor 'prefix blocker'), allowing the advance to proceed. The escape is classified info_only and only fires when a prefix blocker actually exists, never on staleness alone.
summary.why: theoju/engineering-docs-agent had published no documentation since 2026-08-22 (PR #240), with every subsequent nightly run reporting partial and leaving the baseline frozen — a 6-night, growing deadlock (CCE-175). Root cause: a counter cannot be a precondition for its own escape hatch when the counter's persistence depends on the very outcome the hatch is meant to unblock. CCE-140 built the escape but never accounted for state.json's merge-gated write path.

doc_targets.notes: Document the deferral-skip stall clock mechanism (baseline_stall_days, resolve_deferral_stall_days, prefix-blocker forgiveness) alongside existing CCE-140 cursor/deferral documentation.

summary.what_changed: Fixes two bugs in the CCE-175 deferral-skip stall clock discovered on its first production run. First, a run that forgives a stalled PR still reported `advance_cursor_backed = False` in the non-truncated (`else`) advance path, so CCE-140's merge gate (`partial and not advance_cursor_backed`) kept skipping the merge even after the escape fired — the flag is now `bool(skipped_numbers)` so a forgiven run is recognized as cursor-backed. Second, the escape was forgiving every deferred PR in the window rather than only the prefix blocker, which meant first-time deferrals on unrelated PRs got abandoned after 0 consecutive deferrals whenever an earlier PR had stalled the baseline — recreating the deadlock the escape exists to break. The fix narrows forgiveness to the single oldest deferred PR (the actual cursor blocker) per stalled run.
summary.why: CCE-175 shipped a wall-clock escape hatch so a permanently blocked PR can't freeze the baseline forever, since the deferral counter that used to gate the escape only persists on merge (and a stalled run never merges). The first live run to exercise that escape (35609168489, 2026-09-21) showed it fired as designed but still could not merge, and a naive full-window forgiveness policy would re-create the exact deadlock by abandoning unrelated first-time deferrals. CCE-178 corrects both defects, verified against that production run.

summary.what_changed: Appends two new entries to the plugin-conventions list in CLAUDE.md documenting lessons from the CCE-175/178 stall-clock work: (1) the deferral-skip hatch must escape on a wall clock rather than its own counter, since the counter only persists on merge and can never arm during a stall, and (2) a test that reaches its assertion via a different code path than production isn't real coverage, and a design-time prototype that models code instead of running it can confirm a wrong design.
summary.why: CCE-175 and CCE-178 shipped fixes for a baseline deadlock where the deferral-skip escape hatch could never arm because its counter only persisted on merge. CCE-179 captures the two generalizable lessons from that sequence (counters that gate their own escape, and path-divergent test/prototype coverage) so they are recorded durably in CLAUDE.md rather than only existing in spec prose, avoiding the decay mode this project has hit before.

summary.what_changed: page-author's JSON schema now accepts the failure-shape payload it emits when a page can't be authored (null content/page_hint fields) instead of rejecting that payload as schema_invalid. The fix updates agents/schemas/page_author.schema.json and the canonical fenced schema block in agents/page-author.md in lockstep, adds a regression test (tests/agents/test_page_author_failure_payload.py) pinning the documented failure shape as valid, and regenerates the published contract doc.
summary.why: schema_invalid: page-author: None is not of type 'string' fired on 5 of the last 7 nightlies (#267, #268, #270, #272, #275), making it the dominant blocker on the degraded path. The schema required content/page_hint to always be non-null strings, but page-author's own documented failure behavior returns null for those fields when it can't author a page — a shape the downstream consumer already handled gracefully. The mismatch meant the orchestrator's oldest-first admission prefix couldn't document the backlog even when the agent behaved exactly as designed. CCE-180 mirrors the CCE-125 gap-detector pattern of making a schema accept its own documented null/unjudged outcome as first-class rather than as a validation failure.
